Sec. 303 transitional proviso, EO 10084's adoption of existing Pay Readjustment Act regulations (only those to be prescribed by the President) and its March 31, 1950 cut-back bear directly on whether Part D and the amended EO 9871 survived to June 30, 1950
the effect of the statutory repeal and replacement of the order's enabling sections on the amended regulation is neither analysed nor disclosed

defects.claim_says: the 1989 codification note and the 1953 Court rules 'recite the order; neither revokes, supersedes or amends it'
defects.source_says: the OFR 1989 Codification prints EO 10295 as a codified text (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_10295.txt; DISPOSITION_1989.csv: 'Codified at Chapter 32, p. 532', in_force_1989). That book prints only orders still having general effect on January 20, 1989. The claim cites this source as a mere recital and never addresses that the government's own compilers treated the order as in force 38 years after the claimed end.

defects.claim_says: the approval was exhausted on signing; the design 'remained the Court's official seal' only as a consequence
defects.source_says: the order makes the design 'a part of this order' and establishes it as 'the official seal'; the only legal basis for the official-seal status shown in any held source is this order (the 1953 rules cite it as the source). The claim gives no reason why that continuing designation is not a current predicate of the order itself, and its savings text concedes it does not know whether any later instrument changed the seal. Under the 2026-10-28 ruling an endpoint needs a reason that extinguished the command; the contrary 1989 evidence is unaddressed.

defects.claim_says: later_events: []; 'No held order revokes, extends or amends it'
defects.source_says: held EO 10441 (signed March 31, 1953; jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_10441.txt) 'continue[s] in effect until and including July 1, 1953' a subset of the same appointments, namely those of Army and Air Force officers and warrant officers missing, captured or interned, 'which under the following provisions of law would terminate after April 27, 1952, and before July 1, 1953'. It lists the same three statutory provisions, so it carries part of this order's continued appointments past April 1, 1953. Under the production route and the 2026-10-21 ruling, that further extension is a later event with its own date and quote. It does not end this order, but the claim says no such order exists.

defects.claim_says: number-citation, catalog and current-law searches
defects.source_says: EO 10441 does not cite EO 10397 by number, so the number-only searches missed a serial continuation order with a nearly identical title. The searches as recorded were not adequate for a serial continuation order.

defects.claim_says: 1953-12-31: the revocation was performed and the clause spent at the close of business on December 31, 1953; signing and filing are alternative readings
defects.source_says: The order was signed 'Jantiary 19, 1954' and filed 'Jan. 20, 1954; 10:29 a.m.'. Its sentence 'This order shall become effective at the close of business on December 31, 1953' gives the revocation retroactive effect: it fixes when EO 2414 is treated as ceasing. It cannot fix when EO 10514's own command was performed, because the order did not exist on that date. The claim records this order's end 19 days before its issuance, so the lifecycle ends before it begins. The earliest end the source supports for EO 10514's command is its issuance (signing 1954-01-19, or filing 1954-01-20); 1953-12-31 is the end of the revoked order, not of this one.

defects.claim_says: Held EO 10365 (signed 1952-06-24) states that it supersedes Executive Order No. 10266 of June 30, 1951, so far as that order relates to the suspension of certain provisions of the Officer Personnel Act of 1947
defects.source_says: EO 10365 par. 3: 'This order supersedes Executive Order No. 10266 of June 30, 1951, so far as that order relates to the suspension of the operation of provisions of the Officer Personnel Act of 1947, as amended, for commissioned officers of the Marine Corps of the grades of captain and below.' The claim drops the limit to Marine Corps captains and below. As written, the supersession would cover all of EO 10266's subject, since EO 10266 is entirely a suspension of those provisions, and EO 10563's revocation would then have had little or nothing to act on. The source shows that the Navy grades remained under EO 10266 until EO 10563 revoked them.

defects.claim_says: 1958-12-26, the leave direction 'read as tied to the excused day', broader reading disclosed
defects.source_says: The second paragraph directs agency heads to adopt a liberal annual-leave policy for employees 'who wish to take such leave over the holiday period'. The order does not equate the holiday period with Friday, December 26, 1958 (all employees are already excused that day and Christmas is a holiday, so the direction has its effect on other days), and no held source dates the period's end. The claim itself admits 'no held text fixes' the end and describes the broader reading as running to the end of the Christmas and New Year period.

defects.claim_says: 1959-07-03 (close of July 3, 1959): the request 'concerns only that day'
defects.source_says: The held fragment of section 4 requests agency heads to arrange affairs to excuse employees on that day 'or to grant compensatory time m / reof' (in lieu thereof) without additional appropriations. Compensatory time in lieu of an excused day is by nature given on another, later day, and the order states no deadline for it. No held source shows the request ended at the close of July 3, 1959; the endpoint has no reason.

defects.claim_says: 1959-07-03; subsection (b) workday 'ends with it'
defects.source_says: Section 1(b) excuses employees from an entire workday that 'commences on July 2 or July 3, 1959' and covers portions of two calendar days including July 3; a workday commencing July 3 runs into July 4, 1959, so the excusal can operate after the close of July 3.

defects.claim_says: 1960-06-30, the latest clause end
defects.source_says: Because the compensatory-time request has no established end, the latest first end among the clauses (and so the whole-order end) is not established by the held sources.

defects.claim_says: 1959-12-24, the leave direction 'read as tied to the excused day'
defects.source_says: The leave sentence directs a liberal annual-leave policy for employees 'who wish to take such leave over the holiday period'. December 24, 1959 is described by the order as 'the day preceding Christmas Day'; any reading of 'the holiday period' includes at least Christmas Day, December 25, 1959, so the direction cannot have ended at the close of December 24. No held source dates the period's end.

defects.claim_says: A citation search of the 33,118 held order texts ... for the forms Executive Order 11332, Order No. 11332 and E.O. 11332 finds only the capture of the order itself.
defects.source_says: The held-text search returns two files: EO_11332.txt and jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_11331.txt (which prints Executive Order 11332 at line 112 as neighbouring page text). The same rationale says so earlier ('The held-text search also returns the capture file for EO 11331'), and the member earlier_end_check says 'the order own capture and a neighbouring page capture'. The rationale contradicts itself about the search result.

defects.claim_says: 'March 26, 1967 per the held text (the census register lists March 25, 1967 ...)' and, two sentences later, 'Identity: the number, subject and date in the held text agree with the census register.'
defects.source_says: The held text prints 'March 26,1967'. The census register, the OFR catalog and the APP text all give March 25, 1967, and the claim's own signing_date fields are 1967-03-25. The claim asserts that the dates disagree and that they agree, and its prose date (March 26) differs from its structured signing_date (1967-03-25) without saying which is adopted or why.
